mainEntity.name: What if a data set has more than one mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then it is bimodal (two modes) or multimodal (more). This calculator lists every value that ties for the highest frequency. If every value appears exactly once, there is no mode.

mainEntity.name: Why does an extreme value change the mean but not the median?

acceptedAnswer.text: The mean uses every value's size, so one very large number pulls it up. The median depends only on the middle position in the sorted list, so making the largest value larger changes nothing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means?

acceptedAnswer.text: Arithmetic averages values that add, geometric averages values that multiply (such as growth factors), and harmonic averages rates over equal amounts. For positive, unequal values they always satisfy harmonic ≤ geometric ≤ arithmetic.

mainEntity.name: How do I find the median with an even number of values?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sort the list and average the two middle values. For 2, 4, 6, 8 the middle values are 4 and 6, so the median is 5.

mainEntity.name: How does the value:frequency format work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type each distinct value followed by a colon and how many times it occurs, for example 5:2, 8:4 means two 5s and four 8s. The calculator expands it into a full list before working everything out.
A trimmed mean discards a fixed share of the smallest and largest values before averaging. Here 10% is removed from each end, rounded down, so it resists outliers while still using most of the data.
